name: Incomplete or noisy voice input handling
expected: Politely asks user to clarify or re-state the issue without generating hallucinated legal conclusions.
raw_response:
Hello! I understand how stressful it can be when a landlord refuses to return your security deposit, but I am here to help guide you through your rights under Indian law.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant located in Jaipur who is facing an issue where your landlord is unfairly refusing to return your security deposit after the termination of your tenancy. You are seeking a way to recover this amount and understand your rights under Indian law.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state enactments), the security deposit for residential premises is typically capped, and landlords are required to refund the security deposit to the tenant upon taking over vacant possession of the premises.
- Valid deductions from the security deposit can only be made for actual damages beyond reasonable wear and tear, or as explicitly agreed upon under the written tenancy agreement.
- According to Section 108(m) and (o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only bound to restore the property in as good condition as it was at the start, subject to reasonable wear and tear; landlords cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or routine upkeep without a contractual basis.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your signed tenancy agreement, rent payment receipts, the original security deposit payment proof, and photographs or videos of the property's condition at the time of vacating.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your landlord clearly stating the amount due, the basis of your claim, and granting a clear window of 15 days to refund the deposit.
3. Appropriate forum: If the landlord fails to comply, you can approach the local Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal established under applicable state tenancy laws in Jaipur to file a formal complaint for recovery.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. What was the exact amount of the security deposit paid, and for how many months did you reside in the property in Jaipur?
2. Did you sign a written tenancy agreement, and did you receive any written explanation from the landlord regarding why they are withholding your deposit?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
